newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela CenBank to substitute TEMs with T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela CenBank to substitute TEMs with T-bills.

text.p: Venezuela's Central Bank will begin substituting its Monetary Stabilization, or TEM, bills with treasury bills as the main instrument of monetary policy in the next few weeks, a top bank official said.

Congressional approval Wednesday of a bill to refinance $3.7 billion government debt with the Central Bank, paved the way for the bank to start a 450 billion bolivar issue of treasury bills to service the debt, Central Bank first vice president Hugo Romero said.
"We hope the market placements will start in the strictly short term," Romero told reporters in Congress.
The new monetary instrument would relieve the burden of costly weekly TEM bill auctions and make the Bank's monetary policy more efficient.
"They are more classic open market operation instruments," he said.
Romero did not say whether the treasury bills would be placed through auction of by direct placement.
"The issue technique we use will depend on the market situation."
